analogs.covers: Swarm life: a huge, ranked, playful group of tiny scavengers
Strategy: shadowing the big predators for scraps and picking off the helpless

headline: A swarm of rats with a jackal's knack for shadowing the big predators.

setting.label: Everywhere, scurrying between POIs
setting.note: Nomadic. Spends its life moving between POIs and following one trusted large carnivore, most often Tyrannosaurus or Giganotosaurus.

playsLike: You are the smallest carnivore on the roster (Tiny, 400 combat weight) in an unlimited swarm led by one dominant male and several dominant females. You scavenge first and hunt second: unattended babies, Dryosaurus, Psittacosaurus and anything death-scarred, with up to 10 of you on one target. You are fast with enormous stamina (sprint 1,250 for 375 s) and spend your life trailing a trusted giant for scraps.

why.text: Unlimited swarm with one dominant male, several dominant females and challenges for rank. Brown-rat colonies are organised the same way (official inspiration: rats).
Primarily scavenges and 'will do so before attempting to hunt'.
Forms a lifelong 'relationship' with a trusted large carnivore, which shares its kills. Jackals follow lions for the same reason.
Up to 10 in an engagement, but only against Small tier or the helpless.
Highly affectionate and playful, with the fastest land sprint on the roster: 1,250, held for 375 s (jerboa-like, official inspiration).

notLike: Rats don't follow predators, and jackals live in pairs rather than swarms.
twist: The Tyrannosaurus bond works like arctic foxes trailing a polar bear across the ice.
